---
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
\label{_mult_Definition_}
Let  $\pi:\; M {\:\longrightarrow\:} X$ be a proper holomorphic
map, $x\in X$ a point, $F_x:= \pi^{-1}(x)$ 
and $F_i$ its irreducible component, with 
(scheme-theoretical) multiplicity $\mu_i$.
Denote the greatest common divisor of $\mu_i$
by $\mu$. The number $\mu$ is called {\bf the
multiplicity} of the fiber. A fiber is {\bf multiple} if $\mu >1$.
A fiber $F_x$ is {\bf reduced} 
if $\mu_i=1$ for all $i$.
A fiber $F_x$  {\bf has a  reduced component} 
if $\mu_i=1$ for at least one $i$.
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
Let $\pi:\; M {\:\longrightarrow\:} X$ be an abelian fibration
(that is, a fibration with general fiber a complex torus),
and assume that $M$ is K\"ahler. Let $\mu_i$
be the multiplicity of irreducible components
of $\pi^{-1}(z)$ for some $z\in X$,
and $gcd(\mu_i)$ their greatest common divisor. Then $gcd(\mu_i)=\min \mu_i$.
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
Let $\pi:\; M {\:\longrightarrow\:} X$ be an abelian fibration of
complex manifolds
and $D\subset X$ its set of critical values, which
is known as {\bf  the discriminant}, or
{\bf  the discriminant divisor}.
We say that $\pi$ {\bf has no multiple fibers
in codimension 1} if  the fiber $\pi^{-1}(x)$ 
has a component with multiplicity 1 for all
$x$ outside of a codimension 2 subvariety.
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
Let $\pi:\; M \to X$ be an elliptic fibration on a K3 surface.
Then $\pi$ has no multiple fibers.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- head-5: body_md -->
\label{_main_intro_Theorem_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a
Lagrangian fibration on a hyperk\"ahler manifold.
Then $\pi$ has no multiple fibers
in codimension 1.
<!-- end head-5 -->
<!-- head-6: body_md -->
\ref{_no_mult_main_end_Theorem_}. \hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-6 -->
<!-- head-7: body_md -->
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a
Lagrangian fibration on a hyperk\"ahler manifold,
and $\kappa\in H^2(M, {\Bbb Z})$ the fundamental class
of $\pi^{-1}(H)$, where $H\subset {\Bbb C} P^n$ is the hyperplane
divisor. Then $\kappa$ is primitive, that is,
not divisible by an integer $n>1$ in $H^2(M, {\Bbb Z})$.
<!-- end head-7 -->
<!-- head-8: body_md -->
\ref{_primitivity_Theorem_}. \hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-8 -->
<!-- head-9: body_md -->
In \cite{_KV:primitive_}, this result was proven
assuming $\pi$ has no multiple fibers.
However, a Lagrangian fibration
might have multiple fibers in codimension 2, as
I. Hellmann (\cite[Section 2.2]{_Hellmann:cone_}) has shown.
<!-- end head-9 -->
<!-- head-10: body_md -->
Using \cite[Theorem 2.10]{_KL:epiga_non-hyperbolic_},
most of the arguments we use can be extended to the
case where $M$ is a  primitive symplectic variety,
and $\pi:\; M \to X$ a Lagrangian fibration 
with normal base admitting a K\"ahler form on
its smooth locus. We expect \ref{_main_intro_Theorem_}
to be true in this setting as well.
<!-- end head-10 -->
<!-- head-11: body_md -->
In \cite[Theorem 4.12]{_K_Lu:dominability_}, L. Kamenova and S. Lu
prove that for any hyperk\"ahler manifold $M$ admitting a
Lagrangian fibration with no multiple fibers in codimension 1
there exists a holomorphic map ${\Bbb C}^{2n}\to M$
which is locally biholomorphic at some point.
In the present paper we show that this assumption
holds automatically.
<!-- end head-11 -->
<!-- head-12: body_md -->
A {\bf hyperk\"ahler structure} on a manifold $M$
is a Riemannian structure $g$ and a triple of complex
structures $I,J,K$, satisfying quaternionic relations
$I\circ J = - J \circ I =K$, such that $g$ is K\"ahler
for $I,J,K$.
<!-- end head-12 -->
<!-- head-13: body_md -->
A hyperk\"ahler manifold  has three symplectic forms\\
$\omega_I:=  g(I\cdot, \cdot)$, $\omega_J:=  g(J\cdot, \cdot)$,
$\omega_K:=  g(K\cdot, \cdot)$.
<!-- end head-13 -->
<!-- head-14: body_md -->
This is equivalent to $\nabla I=\nabla J = \nabla K=0$:
the parallel translation along the connection preserves $I, J,K$.
<!-- end head-14 -->
<!-- head-15: body_md -->
A holomorphically symplectic manifold 
is a complex manifold equipped with non-degenerate, holomorphic
$(2,0)$-form.
<!-- end head-15 -->
<!-- head-16: body_md -->
Hyperk\"ahler manifolds are holomorphically symplectic.
Indeed, $\Omega:=\omega_J+\1\omega_K$ is a holomorphic symplectic
form on $(M,I)$.
<!-- end head-16 -->
<!-- head-17: body_md -->
A compact, K\"ahler, holomorphically symplectic manifold
 admits a unique hyperk\"ahler metric in any K\"ahler class.
<!-- end head-17 -->
<!-- head-18: body_md -->
A hyperk\"ahler manifold $M$ is called
{\bf of maximal holonomy}, or {\bf IHS}
if $\pi_1(M)=0$, $H^{2,0}(M)={\Bbb C}$.
<!-- end head-18 -->
<!-- head-19: body_md -->
\\
Let $\eta\in H^2(M)$, and $\dim M=2n$, where $M$ is
hyperk\"ahler. Then 
\begin{equation}\label{_Fujiki_Equation_}
\int_M \eta^{2n}=cq(\eta,\eta)^n,
\end{equation}
for some primitive integer quadratic form $q$ on $H^2(M,{\Bbb Z})$,
and $c>0$ a rational number.
<!-- end head-19 -->
<!-- head-20: body_md -->
This form is called
{\bf Bogomolov-Beauville-Fujiki form}. It is defined
by the Fujiki's relation (\ref{_Fujiki_Equation_})
uniquely, up to a sign. The sign is determined
from the following formula (Bogomolov, Beauville)
\begin{align*}  \lambda q(\eta,\eta) &=
   \int_X \eta\wedge\eta  \wedge \Omega^{n-1}
   \wedge \overline \Omega^{n-1} -\\
 &-\frac {n-1}{2n}\left(\int_X \eta \wedge \Omega^{n-1}\wedge \overline
   \Omega^{n}\right) 
\left(\int_X \eta \wedge \Omega^{n}\wedge \overline \Omega^{n-1}\right)
\end{align*}
where $\Omega$ is the holomorphic symplectic form, and 
$\lambda>0$.
<!-- end head-20 -->
<!-- head-21: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a holomorphically symplectic manifold
and  $\pi:\; M \to B$ a holomorphic map. We say that
$\pi$ is {\bf a Lagrangian fibration} if any smooth fiber
$F$ of $\pi$ is a connected holomorphic Lagrangian submanifold of $M$ 
(that is, its dimension is $\frac 1 2 \dim M$ and the holomorphically
symplectic form vanishes on $F$). 
Its {\bf discriminant} is the set of its critical values;
by Sard lemma and Remmert theorem, the discriminant is
a proper complex subvariety in $B$. 
J.-M. Hwang and K. Oguiso prove that the
discriminant of a Lagrangian fibration
is always a divisor 
(\cite[Proposition 3.1]{_Hwang_Oguiso:characteristic_}).
<!-- end head-21 -->
<!-- head-22: body_md -->
\\
Let $M$ be a hyperk\"ahler manifold of maximal holonomy,
and $\pi:\; M {\:\longrightarrow\:} B$ a surjective holomorphic map,
with $0 < \dim B < \dim M$. Then $\pi$ is
a Lagrangian fibration.
<!-- end head-22 -->
<!-- head-23: body_md -->
\\
In these assumptions,  $B$ is biholomorphic to ${\Bbb C} P^n$ 
when it is smooth.
<!-- end head-23 -->
<!-- head-24: body_md -->
The base $B$ 
of a Lagrangian fibration
is biholomorphic to ${\Bbb C} P^n$ when it is normal.
<!-- end head-24 -->
<!-- head-25: body_md -->
In \cite{_CMS-B:AdvStud_}, Cho, Miyaoka, Shepherd-Barron 
stated this conjecture as a theorem, but the proof
had gaps (\cite{_Kebekus_}). When $\dim_{\Bbb C} M=4$, it was proven
in \cite{_Hu_Chenyang:4folds_}.
<!-- end head-25 -->
<!-- head-26: body_md -->
\\
Let $M$ be a hyperk\"ahler manifold of maximal holonomy,
and $\pi:\; M {\:\longrightarrow\:} X$ a Lagrangian fibration, with $X$ normal.
Then $H^*(X, {\Bbb Q})\cong H^*({\Bbb C} P^n, {\Bbb Q})$.
<!-- end head-26 -->
<!-- head-27: body_md -->
\label{_AL_Remark_}
General fibers of $\pi$ are abelian varieties (projective
complex tori), by Arnold-Liouville theorem 
\cite{_Evans:Lagrangian_}. Conversely, as shown by Hwang-Weiss, 
any Lagrangian complex torus in $M$ is a fiber of a Lagrangian fibration
(\cite{_Hwang_Weiss_}).
<!-- end head-27 -->
<!-- head-28: body_md -->
\label{_Huybrechs_chi_Theorem_}
Let $M$ be a hyperk\"ahler manifold, $\dim_C M=2n$
and $L$ a holomorphic line bundle.
Then $\chi (L) = \sum a_i q(c_1(L))^i$, where the coefficients $a_i$ are 
rational constants depending on the topology of $M$.
<!-- end head-28 -->
<!-- head-29: body_md -->
\cite[Section 1.11]{_Huybrechts:basic_}.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-29 -->
<!-- head-30: body_md -->
\label{_chi(L)_Corollary_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to X$ be a Lagrangian 
fibration on a hyperk\"ahler manifold, 
and $L$ a line bundle on $M$ such that
$L^{\otimes d}= \pi^*(L_0)$, for some $d \in {\Bbb Z}$
where $L_0$ is a line bundle on
$X$. Then $\chi(L)=n+1$, where $2n= \dim_{\Bbb C} M$.
<!-- end head-30 -->
<!-- head-31: body_md -->
Since $\chi({\cal O}_M)=n+1$, 
\ref{_Huybrechs_chi_Theorem_} implies that
$\chi(L)=n+1$ for any $L$ such that
$q(c_1(L), c_1(L))=0$. On the other hand,
by Fujiki formula, $q(\eta,\eta)^n= \operatorname{\sf const} \int_M \eta^{2n}$,
and this integral manifestly vanishes for any 
2-form $\eta$ obtained as a pullback from $X$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-31 -->
<!-- head-32: body_md -->
\label{_torsion_free_Claim_}
Let $M$ be a hyperk\"ahler manifold of maximal holonomy.
Then $H^2(M)$ is torsion-free.
<!-- end head-32 -->
<!-- head-33: body_md -->
The universal coefficients formula gives
the exact sequence: 
\[
  0 \to \operatorname{Ext}_{\Bbb Z}^1(H_1(X; {\Bbb Z}), {\Bbb Z}) \to H^2(X; {\Bbb Z}) \to
    \operatorname{Hom}_{\Bbb Z}(H_2(X; {\Bbb Z}), {\Bbb Z})\to 0.
\]
Since $H_1(X, {\Bbb Z})=0$ for a maximal holonomy hyperk\"ahler manifold, 
this gives an isomorphism $H^2(X;{\Bbb Z})=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Bbb Z}(H_2(X; {\Bbb Z}), {\Bbb Z})$,
hence the torsion vanishes.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-33 -->
<!-- head-34: body_md -->
A real $(1,1)$-form $\eta$ on a complex manifold $M$
is called {\bf semipositive} if $\eta(x, Ix) \geqslant 0$
for all real tangent vectors $x$.
<!-- end head-34 -->
<!-- head-35: body_md -->
\label{_DPS_Theorem_}
Let $(M, I, \omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold, $\dim_{\Bbb C} M=n$, 
$K$ its canonical bundle,
and $L$ a holomorphic line bundle on $M$ equipped with a 
Hermitian metric $h$. Assume that the 
curvature $\Theta$ of $L$ is a semipositive form on $M$.
Then 
the wedge multiplication operator 
$\eta {\:\longrightarrow\:} \omega^i \wedge \eta$
induces a surjective map
\[
H^0(\Omega^{n-i}M\otimes  L)\stackrel {\omega^i \wedge
\cdot}{\:\longrightarrow\:} H^i(K  \otimes  L).
\]
Here $\omega$ is considered as an element in $H^1(\Omega^1 M)$,
and multiplication by $\omega$ maps $H^k(\Omega^{n-l}M\otimes L)$
to $H^{k+1}(\Omega^{n-l+1}M\otimes L)$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-35 -->
<!-- head-36: body_md -->
\label{_n+1+H_0_Omega^iotimesL_Corollary_}
Let $L$ be a line bundle on a hyperk\"ahler manifold $M$,
admitting a connection with semi-positive curvature
and satisfying $q(c_1(L),c_1(L))=0$. Then 
$\sum_i \dim H^0(M,\Omega^iM\otimes L)\geqslant n+1$.
<!-- end head-36 -->
<!-- head-37: body_md -->
By 
the ETMDPS vanishing theorem (\ref{_DPS_Theorem_}),
\[ \sum_i \dim H^0(M,\Omega^iM\otimes L)\geqslant \chi(L), \]
and \ref{_chi(L)_Corollary_} implies that $\chi(L) =n+1$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-37 -->
<!-- head-38: body_md -->
\label{_vanishing_filtration_Lemma_}
Let $B$ be a vector bundle equipped with a filtration
$0=B_0\subset B_1 \subset ... \subset B_k=B$.
Assume that $H^0(B_i/B_{i-1})=0$. Then $H^0(B)=0$.
<!-- end head-38 -->
<!-- head-39: body_md -->
The proof is based on induction on $k$ 
and uses the long exact sequence of cohomology
associated with the short exact sequences
$0\to B_{k-1} \to B_k \to B_k/B_{k-1}\to 0$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-39 -->
<!-- head-40: body_md -->
\label{_trivial_on_fibers_Theorem_}
Let $M$ be a hyperk\"ahler manifold admitting a Lagrangian fibration 
$\pi:\; M \rightarrow X$, and $H$ a line bundle on $X$.
Let $L$ be a line bundle such that $L^{\otimes k}=\pi^* H$.
Then $L$ is trivial on all smooth fibers of $\pi$.
<!-- end head-40 -->
<!-- head-41: body_md -->
Let $F$ be a smooth fiber of $\pi$, which is an abelian variety
by Arnol'd-Liouville (\ref{_AL_Remark_}). 
Then $T^*M{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.}$ is an extension
of a trivial bundle $TF$ with another trivial bundle $NF= T^* F$.
For any non-trivial line bundle $L\in \operatorname{Pic}_0(F)$, we have
$H^0(L \otimes TF)=0$ and $H^0(L \otimes NF)=0$,
which implies that  $H^0(L \otimes  T^*M{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.})=0$.
Similarly, one obtains $H^0(L \otimes \Lambda^k T^*M{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.})=0$
(\ref{_vanishing_filtration_Lemma_}).

\hfill
<!-- end head-41 -->
<!-- head-42: body_md -->
Unless $L$ is trivial on $F$, we 
have $H^0(L \otimes \Lambda^k T^*M{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.})=0$,
which implies $H^0(L \otimes \Lambda^* M)=0$.
By the ETMDPS vanishing theorem
this gives $H^i(L)=0$, hence $\chi(L)=0$,
contradicting the formula $\chi(L)=n+1$ (\ref{_chi(L)_Corollary_}).
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-42 -->
<!-- head-43: body_md -->
\label{_primitivity_Theorem_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a Lagrangian fibration
on a hyperk\"ahler manifold, without  multiple
fibers in codimension 1. Then $\pi^*{\cal O}(1)$ 
is a primitive line bundle on $M$.
<!-- end head-43 -->
<!-- head-44: body_md -->
See the end of this subsection. \hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-44 -->
<!-- head-45: body_md -->
\label{_flat_connection_Proposition_}
Let $M$ be a hyperk\"ahler manifold admitting a Lagrangian fibration 
$\pi:\; M \rightarrow X$, and $L_0$ a line bundle on $X$.
Let $L$ be a line bundle such that $L^{\otimes k}=\pi^* L_0$.
Then $L$ admits a Chern connection $\nabla$ which is flat
on each restriction $L{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.}$ to the fiber $F$ of $\pi$.
Moreover, for any closed form $\eta\in \Lambda^{1,1}(X)$
homologous to $\frac{-2\1 \pi}k c_1(L_0)$, $\nabla$ is the unique 
Chern connection on $L$ with the curvature $\pi^*\eta$.
<!-- end head-45 -->
<!-- head-46: body_md -->
Choose a constant metric $h^k$ on $L^{\otimes k}{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.}={\cal O}_F$
and let $h$ be its $k$-th root, which is a metric on $L{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.}$. 
Since  $h^k$ is a constant metric on a trivial line bundle, 
its curvature is flat, and
the Chern connection $\nabla$ associated with $h$ is also flat.

\hfill
<!-- end head-46 -->
<!-- head-47: body_md -->
The last statement of \ref{_flat_connection_Proposition_}
is clear because for every closed $(1,1)$-form $\eta$ homologous
to $-2\1 \pi c_1(L_0)$ there exists a metric
such that the curvature of its Chern connection
is equal to $\eta$ (\cite{_Grif-Har_}). 
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-47 -->
<!-- head-48: body_md -->
\label{_local_mono_Definition_}
We define the {\bf fiberwise monodromy},
or {\bf local monodromy},
of $L$ as the monodromy of $\nabla$ in a neighboorhood of a fiber of $\pi$.
Clearly, the fiberwise monodromy is an invariant
of the line bundle $L$. Moreover, $L$ is a pullback
of a line bundle $L'$ on $X$ if and only if the 
fiberwise monodromy of $L$ on each fiber is trivial.
<!-- end head-48 -->
<!-- head-49: body_md -->
When a fiber $F$ is non-multiple, it is a deformation
retract of its neighbourhood (\cite{_Clemens:degene_,_Persson:degene_}).
When $F$ is a multiple fiber over a general point
of a discriminant, a cyclic covering of its neighourhood 
projects with trivial multiplicity
to a cyclic ramified covering of the base
(\cite[Proposition 3.1]{_Hwang_Oguiso:multiple_}).
In both cases a flat line bundle with trivial local
monodromy is a pullback of a line bundle on the base.
<!-- end head-49 -->
<!-- head-50: body_md -->
\label{_flat_conn_on_restriction_Definition_}
Consider a Lagrangian fibration $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$,
and let $L$ be a primitive line bundle such that 
$L^{\otimes k}=\pi^* {\cal O}(1)$.
Since ${\cal O}(1)$ is trivial on ${\Bbb C}^n={\Bbb C} P^n\backslash H$,
\ref{_flat_connection_Proposition_} also gives a flat connection on 
$L{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{\pi^{-1}({\Bbb C} P^n\backslash H)}}\right.}$.
It can be obtained explicitly as follows.
Let $\nabla$ be the fiberwise flat connection 
defined in \ref{_flat_connection_Proposition_};
its curvature is $\frac 1 k \pi^*\omega_0$, where
$\omega_0$ is the Fubini-Study form on ${\Bbb C} P^n$.
On ${\Bbb C}^n= {\Bbb C} P^n \backslash H$, $\omega_0$ is exact,
$\omega_0= \frac{\1}{2\pi} \6\overline\6 \log\left(1+ \sum_{i=1}^n |z_i|^2\right)$;
let $\theta:= \frac{1}{\pi}d^c \log\left(1+ \sum_{i=1}^n
|z_i|^2\right)$ be its antiderivative. Then
$d(\theta)=\omega_0$. We modify 
$\nabla$ by taking $\nabla_\theta:= \nabla -\frac 1 k \pi^*\theta$,
then $\nabla_\theta^2= \nabla^2- d\theta=0$.
<!-- end head-50 -->
<!-- head-51: body_md -->
\label{_monodromy_then_primitive_Remark_}
If we prove that the monodromy of the flat connection
$\nabla_\theta$ is trivial on $\pi^{-1}(z)$, where $z\in D$
is a general point of the discriminant,
it will follow that it is trivial everywhere. Indeed, 
the fundamental group does not change if
one removes a subvariety of complex codimension 2.
By \ref{_trivial_on_fibers_Theorem_}, the fiberwise monodromy
is trivial on general fibers of $\pi$, 
hence it can theoretically be non-trivial
only on $\pi^{-1}(z)$, where $z\in D$
is a general point of the discriminant.
However, triviality of fiberwise monodromy
of $L$ implies that $L \cong \pi^* \pi_* L$, hence
implies primitivity of $\pi^*{\cal O}(1)$.
Therefore, \ref{_primitivity_Theorem_}
is implied by the following topological result.
Note that we state it for an arbitrary abelian
fibration: the proof is purely topological.
<!-- end head-51 -->
<!-- head-52: body_md -->
\label{_pi_1_preimage_Theorem_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be an abelian 
fibration with no multiple fibers in codimension 1,
and $H \subset {\Bbb C} P^n$ a hyperplane section.
Let $M_0:= \pi^{-1}({\Bbb C} P^n \backslash H)$.
Then the fundamental group $\pi_1(M_0)$ 
is generated by the smallest normal subgroup containing
$\pi_1(F)$, where $F \subset M_0$ is a general fiber of $\pi$.
<!-- end head-52 -->
<!-- head-53: body_md -->
Let $D_0\subset {\Bbb C}^n$ be the discriminant
(that is, the set of critical values) of $\pi:\; M_0 \to {\Bbb C}^n$.
Denote by $X_1$ the complement 
${\Bbb C}^n \backslash D$ and by $M_1$ its preimage in $M_0$.
By \cite[IX, Cor. 5.6]{_Grothendieck:SGA1_}, 
the natural map $\pi_1(M_1)\to \pi_1(M_0)$ is surjective.
However, the map $\pi:\; M_1 \to X_1$
is a Serre fibration with torus fibers,
giving an exact sequence
\[
\pi_1(F) \to \pi_1 (M_1) \to \pi_1(X_1) \to 0,
\]
where $F$ is a general fiber.
The fundamental group $\pi_1(X_1, p)$  of $X_1$ is generated by
the following loops $\Gamma_z$ starting at $p$. We choose a smooth
point  $z$ in $D$, connect $p$ to $z'$ in a small
neighbourhood of $z$ by a path $\gamma_z$. Then we do a small loop $l_{z}$ 
starting and ending in $z'$ and going around $D$ near $z$ and
return back using $\gamma_z$, obtaining $\Gamma_z=
\gamma_z \circ l_z \circ \gamma_z^{-1}$.
<!-- end head-53 -->
<!-- head-54: body_md -->
Let $z''$ be a preimage of $z'$ 
in a neighbourhood of a preimage of $z$
which belongs to a reduced component of $\pi^{-1}(D)$,
and $\widetilde l_z$ a lift of $l_z$
starting in $z''$, going around
$\pi^{-1}(D)$ and getting back to $z''$.
Clearly, its image in $M_0$ is contractible.
<!-- end head-54 -->
<!-- head-55: body_md -->
Since $\pi:\; M_1 \to X_1$
is a Serre fibration with connected fibers,
every path in $X_1$ can be lifted to a path in $M_1$,
and this lift is homotopically unique  up to a 
composition with a loop in the fiber of $\pi$.
Let $\widetilde \gamma_z$ be such a lift of $\gamma_z$.
Then, $\Gamma_z$ can be lifted to a path
$\widetilde \gamma_z\circ A_1 \circ \widetilde l_z \circ A_2  \circ\widetilde \gamma_z^{-1}$,
where $A_i$ are paths in $\pi^{-1}(z')\cong F$ and
$\widetilde l_z$ the loop around a reduced component of $\pi^{-1}(D)$
defined in Step 2. Since $\widetilde l_z$ is
contractible in $\pi_1(M_0)$, we obtain that
$\pi_1(M_0)$ is generated by 
$\widetilde \gamma_z\circ A_1 \circ A_2\circ \widetilde \gamma_z^{-1}$,
where $A_1, A_2$ are loops in a smooth fiber of $\pi$.
This finishes the proof of 
\ref{_pi_1_preimage_Theorem_}.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-55 -->
<!-- head-56: body_md -->
\label{_primitive_multfibers_equiv_Theorem_}
Let $\pi:\; M {\:\longrightarrow\:} {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a Lagrangian fibration
on a hyperk\"ahler manifold of maximal holonomy, 
and $H\subset {\Bbb C} P^n$ a hyperplane section. 
Then the following assertions are equivalent.
\begin{description}
\item[(i)]  The homology class of $\pi^{-1}(H)$ is
primitive.
<!-- end head-56 -->
<!-- head-57: body_md -->
The implication (ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) is proven 
in Section \ref{_primitivity_Section_} using the ETMDPS vanishing theorem.
For the converse implication: let $D_1$ be an irreducible
component of the discriminant $D$; assume it has multiplicity $\mu$.
We need to show that the preimage of the hyperplane section $H$
is not primitive.

\hfill
<!-- end head-57 -->
<!-- head-58: body_md -->
Arguing ad absurdum, 
assume that $\pi^{-1}(D_1)$ is multiple of
multiplicity $\mu$, but $[\pi^{-1}(H)]$ is primitive in
$H_{4n-2}(M, {\Bbb Z})$. 
Clearly, for some $k\in {\Bbb Z}^{>0}$, the divisor $D_1$ is homologous to $k[H]$.
Since $[D_1]= k[H]$, $\pi^{-1}(D_1)$ is the zero set
of a section $s\in H^0({\Bbb C} P^n, {\cal O}(k))$.
The pullback of this section has multiplicity $\mu$;
since $\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$ is primitive, $k$ is divisible by $\mu$.
The universal coefficients formula implies that $H^2(M, {\Bbb Z})$
is torsion-free (\ref{_torsion_free_Claim_}). Therefore, $\pi^*s= s_0^\mu$, where
$s_0\in H^0(M, \pi^*{\cal O}(k/\mu))$. Since $\pi^*{\cal O}(k/\mu)$
is trivial on all fibers of $\pi$, the section $s_0$
is a pullback of a section $s_1 \in H^0({\Bbb C} P^n,{\cal O}(k/\mu))$.
This is impossible, because $s$, and hence $s_1$, vanishes
on $D_1$, which has degree $k$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-58 -->
<!-- head-59: body_md -->
\label{_essential_multiple_Definition_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a Lagrangian fibration,
$L$ a primitive root of $\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$, and
$M_0:= \pi^{-1}({\Bbb C}^n)$ be the preimage of the
complement to a hyperplane. Consider 
the flat connection $\nabla_\theta$ of $L{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{M_0}}\right.}$.
As shown in \ref{_monodromy_then_primitive_Remark_},
$\nabla_\theta$ has trivial monodromy if
and only if $\pi^{-1}({\cal O}(1))$ is primitive.
The union of all irreducible components of $\pi^{-1}(z)$, 
$z\in {\Bbb C} P^n$, for which the fiberwise connection
is non-trivial, is called {\bf an essential
multiple fiber}, and their union {\bf the
essential multiple divisor.} From \ref{_trivial_on_fibers_Theorem_}
it follows that the essential multiple
divisor is a collection of some irreducible components of 
the preimage of the discriminant.
{\bf The order} of the irreducible component of the essential
multiple divisor is the cardinality
of the image of the monodromy of $\nabla_\theta$
in a neighbourhood of $\pi^{-1}(z)$.
<!-- end head-59 -->
<!-- head-60: body_md -->
\label{_essential_multip_Claim_}
Each component of an 
essential multiple divisor is multiple,
and its order is equal to its multiplicity.
<!-- end head-60 -->
<!-- head-61: body_md -->
Let $A$ be an irreducible component of the 
essential mutiple divisor of multiplicity $d$.
Then ${\cal O}(dA)= \pi^*({\cal O}(B))$, where $B=\pi(A)$.
This implies that the bundle ${\cal O}(A)$ admits a section $\nu$
such that its $d$-th 
power $\nu^d$ is a pullback of a section $\nu_1$ of ${\cal O}(B)$.
Since the zeros of $\nu_1$ are of order 1,
the monodromy of $\nu$ along a loop going around $B$ has order $d$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-61 -->
<!-- head-62: body_md -->
\label{_complement_to_C^n_Theorem_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a Lagrangian
fibration, and $L$ a primitive root $\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$,
$L^d=\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$. Then $H^0(M,L)=0$.
<!-- end head-62 -->
<!-- head-63: body_md -->
As we explained earlier in this subsection,
$H^0(M,L)\neq 0$ only if a hyperplane 
$H\subset {\Bbb C} P^n$ is an irreducible component
of the discriminant of $D$ and $\pi^{-1}(H)$
is a divisor of multiplicity $d$. Denote the
 divisor $\frac 1 d \pi^{-1}(H)$ by $H'$.
Clearly, $\dim H^0(M,L)=1$, because
all sections of $L$ vanish on $\pi^{-1}(H)$.
Consider a section of $L$ as a subvariety
$M'$ of a total space $\operatorname{Tot}(L)$.
Clearly, $M'$ is a ramified cover of $M$
of degree $d$, and $H'$ is its ramification divisor.
Consider the Stein factorization of the
projection $M' \to {\Bbb C} P^n$, with
$\pi':\; M' \to B'$ being a fibration
with connected fibers, and $\sigma:\; B'\to {\Bbb C} P^n$
finite. We are going to show that
$\pi':\; M' \to B'$ is an abelian
fibration with no multiple fibers
over a general point of $H$.

\hfill
<!-- end head-63 -->
<!-- head-64: body_md -->
Let $x\in H'\subset M$ be a general point.
Locally around $H'$, the map $\pi$ is written in coordinates as
$(p_1, ..., p_n, q_1, ... q_n)\mapsto (p_1^d, p_2, ..., p_n)$
(\cite{_Hwang_Oguiso:multiple_,_CKV:min_mult_}), where
$p_1=0$ is the equation defining $H'$.
Since $\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$ has zero of order $d$ in $H'$,
the section of $L$ has zero of order 1 in $H'$.
Therefore, after the local trivialization, the global
section of $L$ has the same zeros as the function $p_1$.
This implies that the natural map $M'\to B'$
takes $(p_1, ..., p_n, q_1, ... q_n)$ to $(p_1, ..., p_n)$,
and it is unramified in a general point of $H'$:
we proved the claim made in the end of Step 1.
<!-- end head-64 -->
<!-- head-65: body_md -->
Since $\pi_1({\Bbb C} P^n\backslash H)=0$,
the ramified covering $B'\to {\Bbb C} P^n$ has trivial ramification index.
However, for a general point $x\in H$, the fiberwise
monodromy group of $L$ acts freely on its preimage
in $M'$, because $M'\to {\Bbb C} P^n$ has no multiple fibers
in codimension 1. Therefore, the map $M'\to M$
is a covering outside of codimension 2; this is
impossible because $\pi_1(M)=0$.
This finishes the proof of 
\ref{_complement_to_C^n_Theorem_}.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-65 -->
<!-- head-66: body_md -->
\label{_multiplicities_coprime_Proposition_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a Lagrangian fibration,
and $D_1, ..., D_k\subset M$ are the irreducible
components of the essential multiple divisor
(\ref{_essential_multiple_Definition_}).
Let $\mu_i$ be the multiplicity of $D_i$.
Then the numbers $\mu_i$ are pairwise coprime.
<!-- end head-66 -->
<!-- head-67: body_md -->
Consider the group $\Lambda:= \langle L\rangle \subset \operatorname{Pic}(M)$ generated by 
$L$, which is defined as the primitive root of $\pi^*{\cal O}(1)$.
Then ${\cal O}(D_i)\in \Lambda$, because $\mu_i D_i$ is the
preimage of a divisor in ${\Bbb C} P^n$ (\ref{_essential_multip_Claim_}).
Let $\Lambda_0:= \frac{\langle L\rangle}{\pi^*{\cal O}(1)}$;
by \ref{_torsion_free_Claim_}, this group is cyclic. 
Consider its subgroup $\Lambda_1$ generated by ${\cal O}(D_i)$, 
$i=1, ..., k$. Clearly, this subgroup is also cyclic.
Recall that the Chinese Remainder Theorem implies
that ${\Bbb Z}/{a{\Bbb Z}} \oplus {\Bbb Z}/{b {\Bbb Z}}$ can be realized
as a subgroup in a cyclic group if and only if $a, b$ are coprime.
Therefore, to prove that $\mu_i$ are pairwise coprime, it
suffices to show that 
$\Lambda_0$ is generated by ${\cal O}(D_1)$, ... ${\cal O}(D_k)$,
and relations ${\cal O}(D_i)^{\mu_i}=0$.

\hfill
<!-- end head-67 -->
<!-- head-68: body_md -->
Let $\Lambda_2\subset \operatorname{Pic}(M)$ be the subgroup
generated by ${\cal O}(D_1)$, ... ${\cal O}(D_k)$.
All the relations in $\Lambda_2$ are obtained from 
$Z_1 \sim Z_2$ whenever $Z_1$ and $Z_2$
are zero and pole divisors of a rational
function $f$.  Since the line bundles ${\cal O}_{D_i}$ are trivial on
fibers of $\pi$, these functions
are constant on the fibers of $\pi$,
hence we can assume that $Z_1$ and $Z_2$
are supported on the preimages of divisors on ${\Bbb C} P^n$.
However, after passing from $\Lambda_2$
to $\Lambda_0:= \frac{\Lambda_2}{\langle\pi^*{\cal O}(1)\rangle}$,
the divisors $Z_i$ vanish, hence the only
relations in $\Lambda_2$ are obtained from
taking a power of ${\cal O}(D_i)$ and
obtaining $\pi^*({\cal O}(Z))= {\cal O}(D_i)^{t_i}$;
by definition of multiplicity, this gives $t_i\mid \mu_i$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-68 -->
<!-- head-69: body_md -->
\label{_monodromy_on_torsion_Theorem_}
Let $E$ be a flat complex line bundle
on a manifold $X$. Then $E$ is topologically trivial
if and only if its monodromy, restricted
to the torsion part in $H_1(X,{\Bbb Z})$, is trivial.
<!-- end head-69 -->
<!-- head-70: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{Pic}_{C^\infty}(X)$ be the group
of smooth complex line bundles on $X$.
The exponential exact sequence immediately
implies that an element in $\operatorname{Pic}_{C^\infty}(X)$
is trivial if and only if its first Chern class
is trivial; since $E$ is flat, $c_1(E)$ is torsion.
Let $C(X)$ be the group of characters on
$\pi_1(X)$, that is, the group of homomorphisms
$\pi_1(X) \to U(1)$. We are interested
in the kernel of the natural forgetful map 
$\Phi:\; C(X)\to \operatorname{Pic}_{C^\infty}(X)$.

\hfill
<!-- end head-70 -->
<!-- head-71: body_md -->
The kernel of $\Phi$ consists
of unitary complex local systems with non-trivial monodromy
on a trivial vector bundle, that is, the
maps $\pi_1(X) \to \pi_1(S^1)={\Bbb Z}$.
Clearly, two local systems
$a, b:\; \pi_1(X) \to U(1)$
are topologically isomorphic  whenever
$a b^{-1}$ corresponds to a trivial
line bundle, that is, $a b^{-1}$ is trivial
on the torsion subgroup in $H_1(X, {\Bbb Z})$. 
The restriction of a character
$u\in C(X)$ to the torsion-free part does not
matter for its image in $\operatorname{Pic}_{C^\infty}(X)$, because any homomorphism
${\Bbb Z}^n \to U(1)$ can be lifted
to a homomorphism $Z^n \to {\Bbb Z}$,
hence corresponds to a topologically
trivial line bundle. \hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-71 -->
<!-- head-72: body_md -->
\label{_sections_of_L_otimes_pullback_Theorem_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a Lagrangian
fibration, and $L$ a primitive root of $\pi^*{\cal O}(1)$,
of degree $d>1$. Then $H^0(M, L\otimes \pi^*(L_1))=0$
for all line bundles $L_1$ on ${\Bbb C} P^n$.
<!-- end head-72 -->
<!-- head-73: body_md -->
Let $Z\subset {\Bbb C} P^n$ be an irreducible divisor in 
the complex projective space. It is well known
that $H_1({\Bbb C} P^n\backslash Z)$ is cyclic
(\cite[Chapter 4, Proposition 1.3]{_Dimca:hypersurfaces_}).
By \ref{_monodromy_on_torsion_Theorem_}, this implies
that no trivial line bundle on ${\Bbb C} P^n\backslash Z$ 
can have a flat connection with non-trivial monodromy.
<!-- end head-73 -->
<!-- head-74: body_md -->
Suppose that $H^0(M, L\otimes \pi^*(L_1))\neq 0$.
Since $L\otimes \pi^*(L_1)$ is trivial on general fibers,
the zero divisors of its sections are 
of the form $\pi^{-1}(Z)+ \sum a_i D_i$, where
$Z$ is a divisor on ${\Bbb C} P^n$, and $D_i$
are the irreducible components
of the essentially multiple divisor.
Tensoring with $\pi^*({\cal O}(-Z))$, we obtain
a section of $L\otimes \pi^*(L_1)\otimes \pi^*({\cal O}(-Z))$
which does not vanish outside of the essentially
multiple divisor. This implies that the line bundle
$L\otimes \pi^*(L_1)\otimes \pi^*({\cal O}(-Z))$
is trivial on the complement to the essentially multiple divisor.
<!-- end head-74 -->
<!-- head-75: body_md -->
Let $B:= \pi(D)$, where $D$ is the essentially multiple divisor.
Here we prove that $B$  cannot
be irreducible if $H^0(M, L\otimes \pi^*(L_1))\neq 0$.
Clearly, $D= \frac 1 \mu \pi^{-1}(B)$, 
where $\mu$ is its multiplicity.
 Clearly,  $L\otimes \pi^*({\cal O}(-Z))$
is trivial on the complement to the essentially multiple
divisor, because ${\cal O}(i)$ is trivial on 
 the complement to any divisor in ${\Bbb C} P^n$.
Since $L$ has flat connection on  ${\Bbb C} P^n\backslash B$,
it is trivial on ${\Bbb C} P^n\backslash B$ (Step 1). 
This implies that $L={\cal O}(l D)$, for some integer $l$,
hence $\deg B=1$ and $L= {\cal O}(\frac 1 \mu \pi^{-1}(B))$.
The latter is impossible by
\ref{_complement_to_C^n_Theorem_}.
<!-- end head-75 -->
<!-- head-76: body_md -->
Using Step 3, we obtain that it suffices to prove
\ref{_sections_of_L_otimes_pullback_Theorem_}
when the essentially multiple divisor is not irreducible.
Let $D_1, ..., D_k\subset M$ be the irreducible components
of the essentially multiple divisor, $\mu_i$ the
corresponding multiplicities, and $B_i:=\pi(D_i)$.
Since $\mu_i$ are coprime 
(\ref{_multiplicities_coprime_Proposition_}), for $d:= \mu_2 \mu_3...\mu_k$ 
the bundle $L^d$ is trivial on all $D_i$ except $D_1$;
moreover, this bundle has non-trivial local
monodromy over $\pi^{-1}(z)$, for a general $z\in D_1$.
By the same argument which proves 
Step 2, $H^0(M, L\otimes \pi^*(L_1))\neq 0$
implies that for some line bundle $L_2$ on ${\Bbb C} P^n$
the line bundle $L^d\otimes \pi^*(L_2)$ is trivial
on the general fibers over $B_2, ..., B_k$ and
on the fibers over the complement of $\bigcup B_i$.
Therefore, the bundle $L^d\otimes \pi^*(L_2)$
is trivialized by the section we constructed 
on the complement to $D_1$. 
Since $\pi^*({\cal O}(1)){\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{{\Bbb C}  P^n\backslash D_1}}\right.}$
is trivial, this implies that 
$L^d{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{{\Bbb C}  P^n\backslash D_1}}\right.}$ is trivial,
hence $L{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{{\Bbb C}  P^n\backslash D_1}}\right.}$
is a flat line bundle.
<!-- end head-76 -->
<!-- head-77: body_md -->
Since $d$ is coprime with $\mu_1$, triviality of
$L^d {\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{{\Bbb C}  P^n\backslash D_1}}\right.}$ implies 
triviality of $L{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{{\Bbb C}  P^n\backslash D_1}}\right.}$.
Indeed, if $dd'=1 \mod \mu_1$, we have
$L^{d'}{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{{\Bbb C}  P^n\backslash D_1}}\right.}\cong L{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{{\Bbb C}  P^n\backslash D_1}}\right.}$.
However, 
since $D_1$ is irreducible, any line bundle which
is trivialized on its complement is isomorphic to
${\cal O}(l D_1)$, for some integer $l$.
Then $L={\cal O}(l D_1)$, which is
impossible because $L$ has non-trivial
monodromy over the general points of $D_2, D_3, ..., D_k$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-77 -->
<!-- head-78: body_md -->
Let $F$ be a torsion-free coherent sheaf on $M$.
Define {\bf the degree}
$\deg_\omega F:=\int_M c_1(F) \wedge \omega^{n-1}$,
where $\omega$ is a K\"ahler form. Let
$\operatorname{slope}(F):=\frac{\deg_\omega F}{\text{rank}(F)}$.
A torsion-free sheaf $F$ is called {\bf stable}
if for all subsheaves $F'\subset F$ one has
$\text{slope}(F')<\text{slope}(F)$. If $F$ is  
a direct sum of stable sheaves of the same slope, 
$F$ is called {\bf polystable}.
<!-- end head-78 -->
<!-- head-79: body_md -->
On a hyperk\"ahler manifold of maximal holonomy, 
the bundle $\Omega^{2i+1}(M)$ is stable for all
$i$, and the bundle $\Omega^{2i}(M)$
is polystable.  Moreover, $\Omega^{2i}(M)$
is a direct sum of a stable bundle and ${\Bbb C} \Omega^{i}$,
where $\Omega$ denotes the holomorphically symplectic form.
<!-- end head-79 -->
<!-- head-80: body_md -->
Follows from the Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence
(\cite{_Donaldson:surfa_,_UY_,_Lubke_Teleman:Book_}).
By Calabi-Yau theorem, $TM$ and its tensor powers
admit a Yang-Mills metric, and a Yang-Mills bundle
is polystable, and stable if the holonomy of the
Yang-Mills connection is irreducible. However,
the holonomy of the Yang-Mills connection on
a hyperk\"ahler manifold of maximal holonomy
is $Sp(n)$, and the irreducible decomposition
of the Grassmann algebra for the fundamental
representation of $Sp(n)$ is described in 
\cite{_Weyl:invariants_} (see also 
\cite{_Howe:duality_,_Verbitsky:balanced_,_Verbitsky:SYZ_}).
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-80 -->
<!-- head-81: body_md -->
Clearly, a tensor product of a stable bundle and
a line bundle is also stable.
<!-- end head-81 -->
<!-- head-82: body_md -->
\label{_L_valued_form_non_zero_on_D_Corollary_}
Let $\pi:\; M \rightarrow {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a
Lagrangian fibration, and
$L$ the primitive root of $\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$, such that
$L^d=\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$. Let $u$ a section of 
$L\otimes \Omega^*(M)$.
Then $u$ is non-zero outside of a codimension 2 subvariety.
<!-- end head-82 -->
<!-- head-83: body_md -->
Since $L$ is trivial on any general fiber $F$ of $\pi$
(\ref{_trivial_on_fibers_Theorem_}) the  zero divisor of $u$ is 
the preimage of a divisor $Z\subset {\Bbb C} P^n$.
Indeed, $TM{\left|_{{\phantom{|}\!\!}_{F}}\right.}$ is an extension of trivial bundles,
and any section of its tensor powers is zero or vanishes everywhere.

This implies that the codimension 1 part of the zero set of $u$
is  $\pi^{-1}(Z)$. Then the degree
of the line sub-bundle $V$ of $L\otimes \Omega^{*}(M)$
generated by $u$ is at least 
$\deg \pi^{-1}(Z)= \deg_{{\Bbb C} P^n} Z\cdot  \deg_\omega \pi^*({\cal O}(1))$.
We rescale the K\"ahler form on $M$ in such a way
that $\int_{\pi^{-1}(H)}\omega^{2n-1}=1$, where $H$ is a
hyperplane divisor in ${\Bbb C} P^n$.
This is equivalent to $\int_{\pi^{-1}(Z)}\omega^{2n-1}=\deg Z$
for any divisor $Z\subset {\Bbb C} P^n$. Since $L^{\otimes k}=\pi^*{\cal O}(1)$
and $\deg_\omega \pi^*{\cal O}(1)= \int_{\pi^{-1}(H)}\omega^{2n-1}=1$, we have
$\deg_\omega L= 1/d$.
Then 
\[ 
\operatorname{slope}(V)\geqslant \int_{\pi^{-1}(Z)}\omega^{2n-1} =
\deg Z > \operatorname{slope}(L\otimes \Omega^{2i}(M))=
\deg_\omega L = d^{-1}.
\]
This contradicts the polystability of $L\otimes \Omega^{*}(M)$.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-83 -->
<!-- head-84: body_md -->
From \ref{_n+1+H_0_Omega^iotimesL_Corollary_}, 
we obtain that $\dim H^0(\Omega^* M \otimes L)\geqslant n+1$,
hence the non-zero holomorphic $L$-valued forms exist.
\ref{_L_valued_form_non_zero_on_D_Corollary_} 
implies that these forms might vanish
only in codimension $\geqslant 2$ sets.
<!-- end head-84 -->
<!-- head-85: body_md -->
\label{_diff_forms_to_line_bundle_Proposition_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a Lagrangian fibration
on a hyperk\"ahler manifold, $L^k=\pi^*({\cal O}(1))$
a primitive line bundle, $k >1$. Assume that 
$H^0(L\otimes \Omega^*(M))\neq 0$.
Then there exists a non-zero section on $\pi^*L_1\otimes L$,
where $L_1:= \pi^*(K_{{\Bbb C} P^n}^{-1})$.
<!-- end head-85 -->
<!-- head-86: body_md -->
Let ${\cal F}_1 \subset \Omega^*(M)$ be the sheaf of all
differential forms $\eta$ which are divisible by $\pi^* \Lambda^n {\Bbb C} P^n$,
that is, satisfy $\eta\wedge \pi^*\theta=0$
for any 1-form $\theta\in \Lambda^{1,0}({\Bbb C} P^n)$.
Starting with an $L$-valued differential form $\nu\in H^0(L\otimes \Omega^*(M))$,
we are going to produce a non-zero 
form $\nu_1\in H^0(L\otimes {\cal F}_1\otimes \pi^*(K_{{\Bbb C} P^n})^{-1})$.

Clearly, the sheaf $\Omega^* {\Bbb C} P^n \otimes K_{{\Bbb C} P^n}^{-1}= \Lambda^* T{\Bbb C} P^n$
is globally generated. We are going to multiply $\nu$ by a section
of 
$\pi^*(\Omega^* {\Bbb C} P^n \otimes K_{{\Bbb C} P^n}^{-1})\subset \Omega^* M \otimes\pi^*(K_{{\Bbb C} P^n}^{-1})$
to obtain a non-zero section of ${\cal F}_1\otimes \pi^*(K_{{\Bbb C} P^n}^{-1})$.

Let $dp_i, dq_i$ be a local
frame in a regular point $x\in M$ of $\pi$ such that
$p_i$ are coordinates on ${\Bbb C} P^n$ and the holomorphically
symplectic form is $\Omega=\sum_i dp_i \wedge dq_i$.
Then ${\cal F}_1$ in a neighbourhood of $x$ are differential
forms divisible by $dp_1\wedge ... \wedge dp_n$.
If $\nu$ is locally written as a sum of monomials
on $dp_i$, $dq_i$, which contains a monomial
$dp_{i_1}\wedge ... \wedge dp_{i_a}\wedge dq_{j_1}\wedge ... \wedge dq_{j_b}$,
we can always multiply it by a complimentary monomial on $dp_i$
to obtain $dp_1\wedge ... \wedge dp_n \wedge dq_{j_1}\wedge ... \wedge dq_{j_b}$.
This construction can be applied globally, because 
$\pi^*(\Omega^* {\Bbb C} P^n \otimes K_{{\Bbb C} P^n}^*)$ is globally generated.
Therefore, in the assumptions of 
\ref{_diff_forms_to_line_bundle_Proposition_}
we can additionally assume that $\nu$ is a section
of $L \otimes {\cal F}_1 \otimes \pi^* L_1\subset L\otimes \Omega^*(M)$.

\hfill
<!-- end head-86 -->
<!-- head-87: body_md -->
Let $\nu$ be a non-zero 
section of $L\otimes {\cal F}_1 \otimes \pi^* L_1$.
Denote by $T_\pi M\subset TM$ the sheaf of $\pi$-vertical tangent vectors,
that is, the kernel of $d\pi:\; T_y M\to T_{\pi(y)} {\Bbb C} P^n$,
and let $\Lambda^* T_\pi M\subset \Lambda^* T M$ be the
corresponding sheaf of polyvectors.
We are going to contract $\nu$ with a global holomorphic section of 
$\Lambda^* T M \otimes \pi^* K^{-1}_{{\Bbb C} P^n}$
to obtain a non-zero section of 
$L\otimes \pi^*\Omega^n {\Bbb C} P^n\otimes \pi^*K^{-1}_{{\Bbb C} P^n}\otimes \pi^* L_1=L\otimes \pi^* L_1$,
thus finishing the proof.
<!-- end head-87 -->
<!-- head-88: body_md -->
\label{_no_mult_main_end_Theorem_}
Let $\pi:\; M \to {\Bbb C} P^n$ be a
Lagrangian fibration on a hyperk\"ahler manifold.
Then $\pi$ has no multiple fibers
in codimension 1.
<!-- end head-88 -->
<!-- head-89: body_md -->
By \ref{_primitive_multfibers_equiv_Theorem_}, 
it suffices to show that the line bundle
$\pi^*{\cal O}(1)$ is primitive. Arguing
ad absurdum, assume that $L^{\otimes \mu} = \pi^*{\cal O}(1)$,
where $\mu>1$. By \ref{_n+1+H_0_Omega^iotimesL_Corollary_}, 
the bundle $\Omega^* M \otimes L$
has non-zero sections. 
By \ref{_diff_forms_to_line_bundle_Proposition_},
this implies that $L\otimes \pi^* L_1$
has non-zero sections for some line bundle $L_1$ on ${\Bbb C} P^n$.
However, 
this is impossible by \ref{_sections_of_L_otimes_pullback_Theorem_}.
\hbox{\vrule width 5pt height 5pt depth 0pt}
<!-- end head-89 -->
